caption:
India just started testing the memory chips going into your next laptop. At a $2.75 billion facility built entirely for that one job.

Micron Technology's Sanand, Gujarat facility - India's first commercial semiconductor assembly and test plant - was inaugurated on February 28, 2026, with over 500,000 square feet of cleanroom space. To mark the opening, Micron shipped its first batch of made-in-India memory modules to Dell for India-made laptops. Production is expected to scale from tens of millions of chips in 2026 to hundreds of millions in 2027, serving global customers including Dell, Asus and Qualcomm.

India has designed chips for years. Now it's the place where the world's memory chips actually get finished.

Sources: Micron Technology, Computer Weekly (2026)
